title: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility Wins Earthshot Prize in Mumbai, as Five Winners Take £1 Million Each
excerpt: Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won Clean Our Air at the Earthshot Prize's first India edition in Mumbai; Bhutan, Niue Ocean Wide Trust, PFAS-Free France and Ørsted won the other four £1 million prizes, and Mahila Housing Trust finished as a Fix Our Climate finalist.
body:
• Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won the Clean Our Air prize at the Earthshot Prize Awards Night in Mumbai on Tuesday, November 17, 2026 — the prize's first edition in India and its sixth overall.
  • The other four winners are Bhutan (Protect and Restore Nature), Niue Ocean Wide Trust (Revive Our Oceans), PFAS-Free France (Build a Waste-Free World) and Ørsted (Fix Our Climate); each receives £1 million.
  • India's second finalist, Mahila Housing Trust, did not win — the Fix Our Climate prize went to Ørsted — but remains part of the prize's 15-finalist cohort, chosen from nearly 7,000 nominations across 169 countries.
  • Prime Video streams the ceremony worldwide from November 30, in more than 240 countries and territories and more than 40 languages.

Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won £1 million at The Earthshot Prize Awards Night in Mumbai on Tuesday, November 17, taking the Clean Our Air prize for its electric three-wheelers at the prize's first edition in India. Bhutan, Niue Ocean Wide Trust, PFAS-Free France and Ørsted won the other four prizes, each also receiving £1 million to scale their work. It is the first time the prize — founded by Prince William in 2020 as a decade-long initiative — has held its awards in India, after previous editions in London, Boston, Singapore, Cape Town and Rio de Janeiro.

Prince William and Catherine attended the Mumbai ceremony. William founded the prize to spotlight workable fixes for the planet's environmental problems, and the organisers called the Mumbai ceremony the biggest edition so far.

"Change is not only possible. It is already happening."

— Prince William, founder, The Earthshot Prize, at the Mumbai Awards Night

The five winners

The five winners, announced on the night by The Earthshot Prize, are:

  • Protect and Restore Nature — Bhutan: a nation of 800,000 people, safeguarding water systems for 1.6 billion people downstream across South Asia.
  • Clean Our Air — Mahindra Last Mile Mobility: electric rickshaws powering one of the most rapid and consequential green transitions the planet has ever seen, in the prize's own words.
  • Revive Our Oceans — Niue Ocean Wide Trust: game-changing funding to protect our oceans.
  • Build a Waste-Free World — PFAS-Free France: a people-powered movement to ban “forever chemicals.”
  • Fix Our Climate — Ørsted: transformed from one of Europe's most coal-intensive utilities into a world leader in offshore wind.

Each winner receives £1 million, along with the backing of the prize's Global Alliance of partners. Beyond the prizes, the prize provides all 15 finalists with access to its global network of businesses, investors, philanthropists and environmental organisations. The full winners announcement is on the Earthshot Prize website.

The finalists

The 15 finalists were selected from nearly 7,000 nominations from 169 countries, and are grouped under the prize's five "Earthshots." In Protect and Restore Nature: the Indigenous Desert Alliance, the Yellowstone to Yukon Conservation Initiative, and Bhutan. In Clean Our Air: Satellites on Fire, AirQo, and India's Mahindra Last Mile Mobility. In Revive Our Oceans: the Zero Emission Maritime Buyers Alliance (ZEMBA), the Niue Ocean Wide Trust, and the City of Barcelona. In Build a Waste-Free World: PFAS-Free France, Mother Earth Foundation, and the South Korea Zero Waste Movement Network. In Fix Our Climate: Ørsted, Pula, and India's Mahila Housing Trust.

Earthshot chief executive Hannah Jones called this year's cohort the prize's most globally representative yet, reflecting, she said, the leadership of the Global South and of communities closest to the challenges.

The Indian finalists: one win, one near miss

Mahindra Last Mile Mobility — Clean Our Air — Winner

Led by managing director and CEO Suman Mishra, Mahindra Last Mile Mobility is India's biggest three-wheeler manufacturer — and the only company, and only carmaker, among this year's 15 finalists. It has sold more than 400,000 electric last-mile vehicles, over 100,000 of them in a single year, and says those sales have avoided more than 180,000 tonnes of CO₂. Electric models now account for more than half of all new three-wheeler sales in India, the first vehicle category in the country to cross that line.

The pitch to drivers is economic as much as environmental: lower running costs can lift a driver's take-home income by 25–30%, backed by more than 900 sales and service outlets and access to over 10,000 public charging points. The company has also trained 500 women to drive and repair electric three-wheelers, and is aiming for one million electric vehicles on India's roads by 2031.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=L7w3VkCdOas

Result: winner. Mahindra Last Mile Mobility won the Clean Our Air prize and its £1 million on the night.

Mahila Housing Trust — Fix Our Climate — Finalist

Mahila Housing Trust, led by director Bijal Brahmbhatt, works on the other end of the climate problem: not stopping the heat, but helping the women who live with the worst of it survive it. Its centrepiece is an affordable solar-reflective roof coating that can cut indoor temperatures by up to 5°C in the metal- and concrete-roofed homes of low-income settlements — 36,500 cool roofs so far, demonstrated house by house by women trained as Climate Saathis, and written into Heat Action Plans in cities including Jaipur, Indore and Jalgaon.

Cooling a home does not replace a lost day's wages, so since 2018 the trust has also pioneered parametric climate insurance: when independently measured temperatures cross an agreed threshold, payments arrive automatically, with no loss to prove. Some 49,000 women across Delhi and Gujarat are covered. By 2030 the trust aims to protect three million households and insure 300,000 women.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=bGUnbI-3qQw

Result: finalist. The Fix Our Climate prize went to Ørsted, so Mahila Housing Trust did not win on the night. As one of the 15 finalists, it still gains access to the prize's global network of businesses, investors, philanthropists and environmental organisations.

The night itself

Filmmaker Karan Johar hosted the ceremony, joined by the Prince and Princess of Wales, Sachin Tendulkar, Alia Bhatt, Sonam Kapoor and Rami Malek, with Earthshot ambassadors Robert Irwin and Nomzamo Mbatha also taking part. Five thousand guests enjoyed performances from Shreya Ghoshal, Wild Wild Women, Merlin D'Souza and Simone Ashley, and Take That made their first-ever performance in India, before Shashwat Sachdev brought the night to a finale, according to the organisers. The Serum Institute of India sponsored the Awards Night, and the city was selected during the inaugural Mumbai Climate Week.

What happens next

The five winners each receive £1 million to scale their solution, with the backing of the prize's Global Alliance of partners. For diaspora readers, the full ceremony streams on Prime Video — the event's exclusive streaming partner — from November 30, in more than 240 countries and territories and more than 40 languages, so the Mumbai night is watchable from the US, UK, Canada and the Gulf two weeks after the winners were named. It is not a live stream of the November 17 ceremony.
